_note: Hand-verified REAL, VETERAN-SPECIFIC national resources (hotlines/locators) for categories that have no clean per-place veteran dataset. Each is a genuine VA or veteran-serving org, verified against its official site, and is veteran-specific (not general public). Nationwide referrals carry no coordinates: they appear in every search for their category and place no map pin. Update by editing this file and re-running: node --experimental-strip-types ingestion/run.ts --source curated-national

resources.name: VA Benefits Hotline
resources.description: Call the VA for help with disability compensation, pension, education, and other benefits — what you qualify for and how to apply.
resources.eligibility: Veterans and eligible family members. Free.

resources.name: Find a VA-Accredited Representative
resources.description: VA-accredited Veterans Service Officers (VSOs), attorneys, and claims agents help you file VA claims — VSO help is free. Search the official VA directory.
resources.eligibility: Veterans and dependents filing VA claims. VSO representation is free.

resources.name: County Veterans Service Officer (CVSO)
resources.description: Your county's Veterans Service Officer helps you file for VA benefits in person, for free. Find your local office through NACVSO.

resources.name: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans
resources.description: If you are homeless or at risk of losing housing, call the VA's 24/7 line (1-877-4AID-VET) to reach a trained counselor and local VA housing help.
resources.eligibility: Veterans who are homeless or at risk. Free, 24/7.

resources.name: HUD-VASH Housing Vouchers
resources.description: HUD-VASH combines a rental voucher with VA case management for veterans experiencing homelessness. Ask your VA or the homeless line about eligibility.
resources.eligibility: Veterans experiencing homelessness who qualify for VA health care.

resources.name: Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF)
resources.description: SSVF grantees provide rapid re-housing and homelessness prevention — help with rent, deposits, and utilities — for very low-income veteran families.
resources.eligibility: Very low-income veteran families who are homeless or at imminent risk.

resources.name: VA Grant & Per Diem (Transitional Housing)
resources.description: GPD-funded community agencies provide transitional housing and services for homeless veterans. Ask the homeless line for a program near you.
resources.eligibility: Homeless veterans enrolled in or eligible for VA health care.

resources.name: VA-Accredited Attorneys & Claims Agents
resources.description: For legal help with VA claims and appeals, use a VA-accredited attorney or claims agent. Search the official VA accreditation directory.
resources.eligibility: Veterans and dependents with VA benefit legal matters.

resources.name: Stateside Legal — Legal Help for Veterans
resources.description: Stateside Legal connects service members, veterans, and families to free legal aid, self-help forms, and the Armed Forces Legal Services locator.
resources.eligibility: Veterans, service members, and their families.

resources.name: VA Veterans Transportation Service (VTS)
resources.description: The VA's Veterans Transportation Service offers free rides to and from VA medical appointments. Call 1-800-MyVA411 or ask your VA facility's transportation office.
resources.eligibility: Veterans enrolled in VA health care with a VA-authorized appointment. Availability varies by facility.

resources.name: DAV — Free Rides to VA Appointments
resources.description: Disabled American Veterans runs volunteer drivers who give free rides to and from VA medical appointments at VA locations across the country.
resources.eligibility: Veterans needing a ride to VA medical care. Contact your local DAV Hospital Service Coordinator.

resources.name: Veteran Food & Basic-Needs Help
resources.description: If you're a veteran struggling to afford food, call the VA's homeless/at-risk line (1-877-4AID-VET) — they connect veterans to food assistance and basic needs, even if you're not homeless.

resources.name: Vet Center — Connect to Local Essentials
resources.description: Vet Centers help veterans and families reach local resources — including clothing closets and basic essentials through community and VSO partners. Call 1-877-WAR-VETS.
resources.eligibility: Combat veterans, service members, and their families. No VA enrollment needed.

resources.name: VA Caregiver Support Line
resources.description: Free support for family caregivers of veterans — the Caregiver Support Line connects you with resources and your local support coordinator.

resources.name: Vet Centers — Call 1-877-WAR-VETS
resources.description: Vet Centers offer free, confidential counseling and community for combat veterans and their families. Call 1-877-927-8387 anytime, day or night.
resources.eligibility: Combat veterans, service members, and their families. No VA enrollment needed.

resources.name: Veterans Crisis Line
resources.description: Free, confidential crisis support for veterans and their families, 24/7. Call 988 then press 1, text 838255, or chat online. You don't have to be enrolled in VA care.
resources.eligibility: All veterans, service members, and their families. Free, 24/7.
